scene_description: A small tiled bedroom viewed from an elevated corner, with a bed in the foreground, white shelving and a small cabinet against the back wall, two floor lamps, a doorway, and a white furnishing on the right.
initial_target_observations: The initial reconstruction has a dark, narrow doorway opening but no broad visible door leaf. Consequently it lacks the reference's prominent angled wooden panel and its foreground occlusion.
candidate_target_observations: The candidate adds a light beige, two-panel door leaf in front of the doorway. It is recognizable as a door but appears nearly frontal and much narrower in the image than the reference's strongly angled, larger wooden leaf; its lower edge ends well above the bed instead of extending into the foreground and overlapping the area beside it.
geometric_plausibility_observations: The added panel reads as a freestanding or hinged door in projection, though its hinge and actual connection cannot be established from the image. The reference door has a more oblique silhouette and a much more prominent foreground presence. The candidate preserves the broad placement of the bed, shelves, cabinet, and lamps, but its camera framing and proportions differ from the reference.
new_visible_defects: The newly visible door is flatter and less obliquely oriented in projection than the reference and does not reproduce its foreground overlap. Its pale, uniform surface lacks the reference's visible wood grain.
other_changes: The initial and candidate otherwise appear very similar. Both use flatter, cooler lighting and simpler materials than the reference, with a plain gray floor rather than the reference's mottled floor and rug. The candidate's right-hand white furnishing is only partially visible and differs in silhouette from the reference.

evidence.description: Large angled wooden door leaf extends down into the foreground and overlaps the room view.
Dark doorway opening with no comparably broad visible door leaf.
A pale paneled door now covers the opening, but its projected shape and foreground reach differ from the reference.
White shelving, cabinet and two floor lamps retain the initial arrangement.
Mottled floor and curved pale rug surround the bed and door, unlike the candidate's largely uniform gray floor.

uncertainty: The target is inferred from the visible change between the initial and current images. Different framing complicates exact comparisons of door size and overlap. A single RGB view cannot establish hinge attachment, mesh contact, collisions, hidden geometry, or learned capability.
